description.narrative: Reporting is an important management tool which is used to inform relevant government officials and other stakeholders about the results being achieved by individual projects and the programme as a whole. For project partners, it is compulsory to use the prescribed Orange Knowledge annual report format in order to report on project achievements. The annual report also provides valuable data on the financial situation of the project. Based on an analysis of the project performance in relation to the project output(s) and expected outcome(s), a revision of the project work plan may be suggested by the project partners. The consequences of a possible revision on the project work plan and budget must be made clear in the annual report. Nuffic monitors outputs and outcomes and not activities . Therefore, the main focus of the annual report must be on the achievement of the project’s output(s) and planned outcome(s). The information provided in the annual reports of the projects is used by Nuffic to monitor the progress of the project and to inform the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and other stakeholders about the output(s) and outcome(s) being achieved by individual projects and the Orange Knowledge programme as a whole. Please note that if project progress is in accordance with the original planning, reporting requirements are minimal. Only in case of deviations from the planning, more elaboration is demanded. In the grant award letter, the dates for submission of the annual reports are mentioned. In case of a three-year project, between 5-7 reports are obligatory. The first report (0) is a very short report which focuses on specific conditions and/or recommendations in the grant. There is no need to report on progress in achieving outputs and outcomes, which is done in the first annual report. As annex to the report 0, the consortium agreements between the partners should be submitted. The final report must reflect on the entire project period.

actual.value:
The project aimed to build capacity and increase awareness and skills of students on gender equality and provision of legal aid to clients with gender related problems. In consultation with Nuffic, we revised the approach and included CLAM’s staff as beneficiaries to increase sustainability so that they can provide similar trainings in the future. Also, we changed the beneficiaries from third year students to second year students who will have more time to practice new skills At CLAM during the studies. Below we provide an overview of outputs that envisaged and the results of the indicators.
**Output 1 **_Third year female students have acquired new knowledge and skills to deal with gender sensitive cases during their legal practice at CLAM and after their studies._
_Indicators: _
_**1.**_** **_**# female students that participated in the training and in distance coaching **_
As result of project interventions, 35 2nd year students and 4 CLAM’s staff (lecturers) successfully completed the training course
_**2.**_** **_**# of students that indicates that their knowledge and skills in the trained areas have increased after the training **_
35 students and 4 lecturers have indicated that their knowledge and skills have improved. During interviews and discussion conducted during the training all participants indicated to have increased knowledge and skills. The training provided useful tools on how to conduct interviews with clients and how to increase confidence of female participants. Through exercises and practices during the training sessions, participants could directly apply the new skills.
_**3.**_** **_**Training materials on interview techniques and gender mediation skills available for current and future use.**_
Training materials have been made and provided during and after the training sessions for participants to access and use
​
**Output 2** Third year female students are aware of gender equality and women’s rights and are capable to defend these rights during their studies and in their career.
**1. Female students have acquired the skills to stand out and advocate for change and safeguarding gender equality and women rights **
_The 35 Female students and 4 lecturers who pursued the training course have upscaled their skills and capacity and can standout with confidence to combat gender inequality in their environment _
**2. Materials and # tools available for use in current and future trainings **
For all training sessions, materials, presentations and handouts were provided so that the participants can make use of them in the future
**3. Improved students reports and confidence of clients on CLAM’s services**
_So far, clients have been satisfied with the services provided by CLAM as the legal aid provided by students and lecturers has improved _

comment.narrative: 19-12-2022: As the title suggests (FEMALE project), this project focused only female candidates. The main objective was to build capacity of female staff of CLAM (Center for Legal Aid and Mediation at University of Rwanda). Measures that were adopted to stimulate supervision and aftercare of female candidates are many. This include: - Coaching and leadership skills training of candidates which gives them more confident on providing suitable legal aid - Gender awareness training for CLAM staff and students - Mediation skills training for CLAM’s staff and students so that they hand make good referrals for clients of legal aid - Interview techniques so that they can interview gender sensitive clients
